panels.title: Poll Success Rate
panels.description:
Share of poll ticks that finished without throwing, over the range.

When bad: below ~95% means poll() calls are erroring — check Errors by Kind. One node type is a node/credential bug, all types point to network or the source systems.

targets.query:
import "array"

every = if int(v: v.windowPeriod) > int(v: 1m) then v.windowPeriod else 1m

from(bucket: "${bucket}")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "n8n" and (r._field == "n8n_poll_trigger_duration_seconds_count"))
  |> filter(fn: (r) => contains(value: r["node_type"], set: ${node_type:json}))
  |> filter(fn: (r) => contains(value: r["url"], set: ${instance:json}))
  |> increase()
  |> last()
  |> group()
  |> reduce(
    identity: {ok: 0.0, total: 0.0},
    fn: (r, accumulator) => ({
      ok: accumulator.ok + (if r.status == "success" then r._value else 0.0),
      total: accumulator.total + r._value,
    }),
  )
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({"Poll Success Rate": if r.total > 0.0 then r.ok / r.total else 0.0}))

panels.title: Poll Rate
panels.description: Poll ticks per second, across all mains.

targets.query:
import "array"

every = if int(v: v.windowPeriod) > int(v: 1m) then v.windowPeriod else 1m

from(bucket: "${bucket}")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "n8n" and (r._field == "n8n_poll_trigger_duration_seconds_count"))
  |> filter(fn: (r) => contains(value: r["node_type"], set: ${node_type:json}))
  |> filter(fn: (r) => contains(value: r["url"], set: ${instance:json}))
  |> aggregateWindow(every: every, fn: last, createEmpty: false)
  |> derivative(unit: 1s, nonNegative: true)
  |> group(columns: ["_time"])
  |> sum()
  |> group(columns: [])
  |> keep(columns: ["_time", "_value"])
  |> rename(columns: {_value: "Poll Rate"})

panels.title: Overlapping Ticks (range)
panels.description:
Ticks that started while another tick for the same node was still in flight in the same process, over the range.

When bad: any overlap means a poll runs longer than its interval — check Poll Duration p99 for that node type and consider a longer interval or poll timeout.

targets.query:
import "array"

every = if int(v: v.windowPeriod) > int(v: 1m) then v.windowPeriod else 1m

union(tables: [
  from(bucket: "${bucket}")
    |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
    |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "n8n" and (r._field == "n8n_poll_trigger_overlapping_ticks_total"))
    |> filter(fn: (r) => contains(value: r["node_type"], set: ${node_type:json}))
    |> filter(fn: (r) => contains(value: r["url"], set: ${instance:json}))
    |> increase()
    |> last()
    |> group()
    |> keep(columns: ["_value"]),
  array.from(rows: [{_value: 0.0}]),
])
  |> group()
  |> sum()
  |> rename(columns: {_value: "Overlapping Ticks (range)"})

panels.title: Fence Rejections (range)
panels.description:
Cursor writes rejected by the scheduler-lease fence over the range — a poll losing the race against a reclaimed lease. No node_type label; only the instance filter applies.

When bad: each rejection is a prevented duplicate — expected occasionally under lease churn. A sustained rise means mains are losing leases mid-poll; check Duplicate-Risk Signals and main health.

targets.query:
import "array"

every = if int(v: v.windowPeriod) > int(v: 1m) then v.windowPeriod else 1m

    |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "n8n" and (r._field == "n8n_poll_trigger_cursor_commits_total") and r.result == "fence_rejected")
    |> filter(fn: (r) => contains(value: r["url"], set: ${instance:json}))
    |> increase()
    |> last()
    |> group()
    |> keep(columns: ["_value"]),

  |> sum()
  |> rename(columns: {_value: "Fence Rejections (range)"})

panels.title: Poll Duration — p50 / p90 / p99
panels.description:
Duration of the poll() call itself, from the shared choke point of the cron and durable paths. Baseline for tuning the poll-timeout default.

When bad: p99 approaching the poll interval causes overlapping ticks; p99 diverging while p50 stays low means one source system is slow — compare by node type.

panels.title: Errors by Kind
panels.description:
Poll ticks that threw, per second, classified from the source's HTTP status: auth (401/403), rate_limited (429), or thrown (anything else).

When bad: auth means a broken credential — permanent until fixed, disable or re-auth the workflow. rate_limited means the interval is too aggressive for the source. thrown is transient or a node bug — check the logs.

panels.title: Duplicate-Risk Signals — Overlap, Lease Loss & Fence Rejections
panels.description:
The three signals that measure the residual-duplicate risk. Overlapping ticks: same-process overlap. Lease lost: a handler finished after its lease was reclaimed (cross-main overlap window). Fence rejected: a cursor write from such a handler was blocked.

When bad: lease losses without matching fence rejections are the unprotected window — the data that decides whether cross-process cursor fencing is worth closing now.

panels.title: Cursor Commit Outcomes
panels.description:
Poll-cursor commits per second by result. with_execution commits the cursor and the execution in one transaction; cursor_only advances the cursor without new items. No node_type label.

When bad: failures mean the cursor transaction is not committing (DB errors, contention) — polls will re-see items. Fence rejections are prevented duplicates; see Duplicate-Risk Signals.

panels.title: Cursor Commit Latency — p50 / p99 by Operation
panels.description:
Latency of poll-cursor commits by operation. with_execution includes the execution insert, so it is expected to be slower than cursor_only. No node_type label.

When bad: rising latency means DB pressure on the poller-state table — it delays the next tick and widens the overlap window.
